answer: Like a jetty that lets only one boat dock at a time, an agent economy can charge every action a small refundable deposit, returned after a short cooldown unless fraud is reported. Honest agents barely notice the fee, it flows back like the tide. A Sybil farm faces a different ocean: thousands of fake identities must each lock capital, and rapid-fire actions escalate both the deposit and the wait, so at dawn its funds are still tied up while real work has already sailed through. Attack cost scales with identities; honest cost stays near zero.
